subject: Privacy carve-out: prompt custody & model-improvement opt-out — sprint plan
messages:
From: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@medovahealth.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
Cc: Emma Patel <emma@medovahealth.com>, DevOps Team <devops@medovahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifying DPA carve-out: no-train + prompt custody

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for the redline. Legal had a couple of high-level asks before we move this into procurement:

1) Medova needs a firm operational path for a no-training (no-model-improvement) commitment — not just a promise in the DPA. We need to confirm: where will customer interaction data (prompts + responses) be stored, how long retained, and whether any telemetry/aggregates might ever be used for model tuning.

2) Prompt/response custody: customers want an explicit carve-out that the customer retains IP over prompts and model outputs for the tenant’s own data. We expect a short ops runbook and a delivery milestone in the contract that shows how you enforce that for hosted and dedicated deployments.

3) Subprocessors: need an inventory (including region of processing) and an indication which subprocessors will process logs/payloads for hosted API versus Dedicated vs Private.

Can you share a proposed implementation plan & evidence items we can attach to the DPA? Example items that would help: a short runbook, a list of retention TTLs, and a diagram showing dataflow for both hosted and dedicated modes (SFTP/Onshore KMS path).

We’re trying to land procurement next week, so quick turn appreciated.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Ramos | Counsel, Data & Privacy
Medova Health

Attachments: Medova_DPA_v1.pdf
From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@medovahealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying DPA carve-out: no-train + prompt custody

Hi Alicia — thanks, this is helpful and fair. Summarizing how Redwood proposes to operationalize the commitments (short version):

Operational guarantees we can commit to (hosted & dedicated):
- No-model-improvement (No-Train): Customer data marked as "no-train" will be excluded from all model-improvement pipelines (both online and offline). No-derived parameter updates will use these inputs.
- Prompt/Response custody: Customers retain output IP; we will store prompt/response payloads in tenant-scoped storage with per-tenant encryption keys.
- Retention & TTLs: Default hosted retention for payloads = 30 days; we can configure Dedicated to meet customer-specified TTLs (e.g., 0–365 days) as part of onboarding.

Evidence and runbook deliverables we can provide this week:
- 1-page No-Train Ops Runbook (how we tag traffic, routing rules, proof artifacts) — will include CLI snippet + API call examples.
- Subprocessor inventory CSV with processing region columns (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Dataflow diagrams for Hosted vs Dedicated (SFTP export lane + onshore KMS path).
- Exportable proof package: sample audit log extract showing a "no-train" tag and confirmation that the payload did not hit improvement pipelines. (redacted/example data)

Asks from your side to make the docs actionable for procurement:
- Confirm desired retention TTL for the Dedicated environment (if different from 30d).
- Confirm whether the legal team needs a signed attestation for subprocessors (we can provide quarterly attestation).
- Let us know if you want KMS-in-customer-control for Dedicated or Private.

I’ll loop in Kimberly for the proof package and Jordan for the DPA redline items we need to align on.

Thanks — I’ll send the runbook + inventory by EOD.

— Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma | Senior Manager, Security & Privacy Operations
Redwood Inference
